subject.title: feat: version field in health response + POST /admin/update endpoint

question: Should OpenClaw expose host update execution to HTTP fleet tooling, and if so should it be through the opt-in Admin HTTP RPC allowlist or a dedicated `POST /admin/update` endpoint?
rationale: Current main intentionally keeps health probes shallow and keeps `update.run` out of the Admin HTTP RPC allowlist; changing either surface affects public metadata and trusted operator control-plane security.

options.title: Version only, no HTTP update yet
options.body: Keep the version metadata decision on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91795 and defer or reject HTTP-triggered updates until a stronger security design is approved.

options.title: Expose update.run through Admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Add `update.run` to the existing opt-in `/api/v1/admin/rpc` allowlist with explicit private-ingress docs, tests, rate-limit coverage, and update/restart proof.

options.title: Design a dedicated update endpoint
options.body: Create a purpose-built `POST /admin/update` contract only if maintainers want a simpler fleet API separate from generic Admin HTTP RPC.

recommendation.title: Version only, no HTTP update yet
recommendation.body: Keep the version metadata decision on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91795 and defer or reject HTTP-triggered updates until a stronger security design is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: The most sensitive remaining decision is update execution over an admin surface, and Peter introduced the Gateway update restart flow plus adjacent version helper work.
